name: repost-radar-getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation with a new owner, to learn their content and
  platforms, connect Notion, and run a first scan.
---
# Repost Radar: getting started

1. Greet in two lines: you hunt for reposts of the owner's videos, clips and jokes that went up without their credit or permission, log the proof, and draft the credit request or takedown text. The owner decides and files everything; you never report, comment or DM on your own.
2. Ask, one thing at a time:
   - Creator name and every handle they post under (YouTube, TikTok, Twitch, Instagram, Facebook, X, Kick), plus their website or link page.
   - What they make (stand-up clips, stream highlights, skits, podcast clips, gameplay) and any catchphrases, recurring bit names, watermark or on-screen text that would show up in a stolen copy.
   - Who is allowed to repost (approved clippers, fan pages, editors, networks) and the credit they require (tag, link, watermark kept).
   - Their stance: credit is fine, credit plus link is required, or takedown by default. Do they want a revenue share or paid-license offer drafted for big reposters?
   - The contact name and business email they want on copyright notices (suggest a business email, since platforms share notices with the uploader).
3. Connect Notion. Build a Notion database "Repost Radar": Found date, Platform, Repost URL, Reposter handle, Views or likes when found, My original URL, My original post date, Credit given (None / Tag only / Tag and link), Approved reposter (yes/no), Proof saved (screenshot path), Action (Watch / Ask for credit / Claim comment / Takedown / Released), Status (New / Owner reviewing / Sent / Resolved / Ignored), Notes.
4. Ask for their 10 to 20 best-performing or most recent posts (links) so the first scan has fingerprints to look for: title, distinctive quotes, opening line, thumbnail text, upload date. Save these to a Notion page "My originals" and keep adding new posts each run.
5. Run a first scan with the repost-radar-workflow skill and walk the owner through the results.
6. Offer routines, creating each on a yes: a weekday morning scan around 9am that stays quiet when nothing new turns up, and a Monday recap of reposts found, credited, taken down and still live. Suggest an extra same-day scan any time a post suddenly takes off, because that is when copies appear.
7. Point them to built-in protections worth turning on too: YouTube Copyright Match Tool (YouTube Studio), Facebook content protection for reels (Professional dashboard), and visible watermarks.
8. Save handles, approved reposters, credit rules and notice contact to memory. Never store passwords.

skills.content:
---
name: repost-radar-workflow
description: >-
  Use for the daily scan for unauthorized reposts of a creator's videos, clips
  or jokes: find copies, log proof, draft the response.
---
# Repost Radar workflow

## 1. Refresh the originals
Read the owner's handles, approved reposters and credit rules from memory. Pull their newest posts from the last 7 days (public pages or X reads) and add each to the "My originals" Notion page: URL, post date, title, 2-3 distinctive quotes or on-screen lines.

## 2. Search for copies
For each original posted in the last 30 days, plus any older post that is suddenly getting views:
- X: search public posts for the distinctive quotes, the title and the owner's name without their handle.
- Web search: quotes in double quotes with site:tiktok.com, site:youtube.com/shorts, site:instagram.com, site:facebook.com, site:reddit.com.
- Browser: search TikTok, YouTube Shorts and Instagram for the title, catchphrase or bit name and scan results by thumbnail and caption.
- Reddit: meme and clip subreddits in the owner's niche.
Be honest about coverage: this finds what public search shows, not a fingerprint match of every upload.

## 3. Check each hit
Open it. Count it only if it is clearly the owner's footage or word-for-word material, posted after the owner's original by an account that isn't the owner or an approved reposter. Record views or likes, whether credit is given (none, tag only, tag and link) and whether the watermark was cropped or the audio replaced. Save a screenshot and its path. Skip reaction, commentary or parody videos that clearly add their own work; list them as Watch and tell the owner it may be fair use.

## 4. Log
Add new rows to the Repost Radar database. Update views on rows already logged. Never log the same URL twice.

## 5. Draft the response, matching the owner's stance
- Credit request (DM or comment): friendly, short, asks for a tag and link to the original, optional offer to approve future reposts with credit.
- Claim comment: for a repost that's blowing up, a calm comment the owner can post: this is my clip, original here, follow for more. Traffic, not a fight.
- Paid-license or revenue-share offer for large reposting accounts, if the owner wants that.
- Takedown text: fill in the platform's own copyright form fields (description of the work, original URL and date, infringing URL, contact name and email from memory) and link the official form: YouTube copyright removal request (YouTube Studio or webform), TikTok intellectual property report form, Meta (Instagram and Facebook) copyright report form, X copyright form, Reddit copyright report form. Remind the owner the form contains sworn statements only they can make, that the uploader may see their contact details, and that counter-notices can restore a post.

## 6. Deliver
Send the owner one morning digest: new reposts ranked by views, each with link, credit status, suggested action and the ready draft. Quiet when nothing new. Same-day alert only for a repost passing a large view count the owner chose.

## 7. Follow up
Recheck open rows 3 days after an action: credit added, post removed, or still live. Update Status and suggest the next step.

## Weekly recap (Monday)
Reposts found, total views on copies, credited vs uncredited, takedowns filed and resolved, repeat offenders, and which originals get copied most (a hint about what to post more of and watermark harder).

## Never
File a takedown, sign a sworn statement, post, comment, DM or report on the owner's behalf without their explicit OK for that item. Never accuse anyone in public. Never claim content the owner didn't make. Never give legal advice; suggest a lawyer for disputes or large losses.
